proposals.before: Soon Wang Dao dispatched eight regional inspectors; Gu He came back from the outer circuits with their reports and was admitted with the rest. Every inspector aired complaints about the commandery governors—only Gu He stayed silent.
proposals.after: Soon Wang Dao dispatched eight department aides on inspection tours; Gu He came back from the outer circuits with their reports and was admitted with the rest. Every aide aired complaints about the commandery governors—only Gu He stayed silent.
proposals.reason: 八部從事 are department aides, not regional inspectors; the idiomatic rendering invents the wrong office.

proposals.before: Early in Taining, Wang Dun took him on as chief clerk; he rose to gentleman-attendant at the heir’s palace, then adviser on the staff of the chariot-and-cavalry general and chief clerk to the Defender-in-Chief.
proposals.after: Early in Taining, Wang Dun took him on as chief clerk; he rose to gentleman-attendant at the heir’s palace, then adviser on the staff of the chariot-and-cavalry general and chief clerk to the Army Protector.
proposals.reason: 護軍長史 is chief clerk to the Army Protector (護軍), not to the Defender-in-Chief (太尉).

proposals.before: In the early Taining era Wang Dun requested him as chief clerk; he was promoted to attendant of the heir apparent, army adviser to the chariot and cavalry general, and senior clerk to the Defender-in-Chief.
proposals.after: In the early Taining era Wang Dun requested him as chief clerk; he was promoted to attendant of the heir apparent, army adviser to the chariot and cavalry general, and senior clerk to the Army Protector.
proposals.reason: The literal likewise mistranslates 護軍 as Defender-in-Chief.
袁瑰 is Gui, not Mei; the heading romanization is a name error.
The literal heading repeats the same wrong romanization of 瑰.

proposals.before: The Prince of Donghai’s body had been cremated by Shi Le; Lady Pei asked to bury a soul-summoning garment in lieu of remains, and ministers hesitated.
proposals.after: The Prince of Donghai, Yue, had already had his corpse burned by Shi Le; his consort Lady Pei asked to bury a soul-summoning garment in lieu of remains, and ministers hesitated.
proposals.reason: Idiomatic English omits the personal name Yue (越) present in the Chinese 東海王越 and the prior-aspect 既, and it drops 妃 identifying Lady Pei as the prince’s consort.

proposals.before: Courtesy now narrows what old camaraderie allowed; the reproof for sprawling discourtesy shifts with the times—there is no going back to abstract chatter about Carefree Roaming and shedding ritual.
proposals.after: Courtesy now narrows what old camaraderie allowed; the reproof for sprawling discourtesy shifts with the times—there is no going back to abstract chatter about Zhuangzi’s Hao-river debates and shedding ritual.
proposals.reason: 濠肆 refers to the Hao River setting of Zhuangzi, not the chapter title Carefree Roaming (逍遙遊). The literal already renders riverside freedom.

proposals.before: You bore the courtesy name Shenfu and was as celebrated as his elder brother in youth.
proposals.after: You bore the courtesy name Shenfu and in youth shared Mei’s reputation.
proposals.reason: The Chinese names 瑰 in this sentence; the idiomatic line replaces that personal name with a kinship paraphrase.

proposals.before: In Su Jun’s coup Wang Dao enlisted him as adviser and kept him at Stone fortress.
proposals.after: In Su Jun’s coup Wang Dao enlisted him as adviser, and he accompanied Dao at Stone fortress.
proposals.reason: 隨導在石頭 means Dan followed Wang Dao at Shitou, not that Dao kept him there.

proposals.before: Jiang You advanced his troops to Yao Xiang’s camp and told the officers: “Our troops are not unfit, but we are fewer than the Qiang and their ditches and palisades are strong—hard to match strength head-on; I shall defeat them by stratagem.
proposals.after: Jiang You advanced his troops to Yao Xiang’s camp and told the officers: “Our troops are not unfit, but we are fewer than the Qiang and their ditches and palisades are strong—hard to match strength head-on; I shall defeat them by stratagem.”
proposals.reason: The literal English leaves the quoted speech unclosed.

proposals.before: Emperor Kang’s burial first introduced jeweled blades and gold slippers—emotion overrode precedent and broke generations of restraint.
proposals.after: Emperor Kang’s burial first introduced jeweled blades and gold slippers—the grand consort’s unbounded grief overrode precedent and broke generations of restraint.
proposals.reason: Idiomatic English drops 太妃, the named agent of the emotion that violated ancestral burial law.

proposals.before: When Prince Yuanxian of Kuaiji seized power and opened the six palace gates at night Ji secretly urged Prince Daozi to report it—Daozi refused.
proposals.after: When the heir apparent of Kuaiji, Yuanxian, seized power and opened the six palace gates at night Ji secretly urged Prince Daozi to report it—Daozi refused.
proposals.reason: 會稽世子元顯 is the heir apparent of the Prince of Kuaiji, not himself Prince of Kuaiji (that title belongs to 會稽王道子 in the same sentence).

proposals.before: Under Taiyuan the academy added a hundred students and named Yin their doctoral libationer.
proposals.after: During the Taiyuan era they added a hundred National Academy students and placed Yin in charge as erudit of the National University.
proposals.reason: 領國子博士 is directing as a National University doctor, not the libationer (祭酒).

proposals.before: His ancestor Yin Rong led the Chamberlain’s office.
proposals.after: His grandfather Yin Rong led the Chamberlain’s office.
proposals.reason: 祖 denotes the grandfather, not a generic ancestor.

proposals.before: His ancestor Rong had been Chamberlain for Ceremonial.
proposals.after: His grandfather Rong had been Chamberlain for Ceremonial.
proposals.reason: 祖 denotes the grandfather, not a generic ancestor.

proposals.before: Wang Ya, courtesy Maoda, came from Tan in Donghai—descended from Wang Su, Wei’s guard-general of the right.
proposals.after: Wang Ya, courtesy Maoda, came from Tan in Donghai—descended from Wang Su, Wei’s Guard General.
proposals.reason: 衛將軍 is General Who Guards; the translation invents “of the right.”

decisions.reason: 八部從事 are circuit department clerks/aides sent out 之部, not 刺史-grade regional inspectors; replacing inspector with department aide restores the office.

sourceWitness.excerpt: 導遣八部從事之部……諸從事各言二千石官長得失

decisions.reason: 護軍長史 is senior clerk to the Army Protector (護軍), not to the Defender-in-Chief (太尉); the proposed office title matches the Chinese.
The literal line makes the same 護軍/太尉 substitution; Army Protector is the correct rendering.
The given name 瑰 is Guī, not Méi; the heading romanization is a naming error.
The literal heading repeats the same false Méi reading of 瑰; Gui is required.
The Chinese names 東海王越, marks the burning as already done with 既, and identifies 妃裴氏 as his consort; the repair restores those elements without changing the rest of the human wording.

sourceWitness.excerpt: 東海王越屍既為石勒所焚，妃裴氏求招魂葬越

decisions.reason: 虛詠濠肆 alludes to Zhuangzi’s Hao-river (濠) free talk, not the chapter title 逍遙遊; the replacement corrects the allusion.

decisions.after: You bore the courtesy name Shenfu and in youth was as celebrated as Gui.
decisions.reason: 少與瑰齊名 does name 瑰, so the kinship-only original is incomplete, but the proposal’s Mei repeats the false romanization of 瑰 already rejected at the heading.
隨導在石頭 makes Yuan Dan the one who accompanied Wang Dao at Stone fortress; “kept him” reverses the agency.
The Chinese speech is a complete quoted utterance (謂將校曰「……」); closing the English quotation is required and changes no meaning.

sourceWitness.excerpt: 謂將校曰：「今兵非不精……吾當以計破之。」

decisions.reason: 此蓋太妃罔已之情 names the grand consort as the agent of the grief that broke burial law; omitting 太妃 leaves the emotion unattributed.
會稽世子元顯 is the heir apparent; 會稽王 belongs to 道子 in the same sentence, so “Prince Yuanxian of Kuaiji” is a title error.

sourceWitness.excerpt: 會稽世子元顯專政……密啟會稽王道子

decisions.after: During the Taiyuan era they added a hundred National Academy students and placed Yin in charge as erudite of the National University.
decisions.reason: 領國子博士 is concurrent charge as National University erudite (博士), not 祭酒; “erudit” in the proposal is not English for that office.
祖融, paired with 父康 in the next sentence, is Yin Yi’s grandfather, not a vague ancestor.
The literal likewise renders 祖 as ancestor; grandfather is the kinship term required by 祖融.
魏衛將軍肅 is Guard General; 右 is not in the Chinese, so “of the right” is invented.

claimRevisions.reason: The heading 袁瑰 supports English Gui, matching the already-correct pinyin Yuán Guī; Mei is only a mistranslation.
The given-name graph 瑰 in this unit is Gui; both the English Mei and pinyin Mei come from the bad romanization.
The inferred personal name built on 瑰 must follow Gui, not Mei.

dateContext.event: Kept at Stone fortress during Su Jun’s rising.
Accompanied Wang Dao at Stone fortress during Su Jun’s rising.

claimRevisions.reason: Presence at 石頭 is still in the source, but “kept/posted” was created by the mistranslation of 隨導; he accompanied Dao there.
